name: Patchline Rivet-Stud Utility Belt
description:
Assembled from salvaged conveyor-belt rubber and reclaimed nylon webbing, this wide utility belt is studded with mismatched brass and steel rivets — each one a different origin. Pouches are heat-sealed scrap vinyl, secured with scavenged buckles. Acid-bleach patterns streak the main strap in pale yellow-grey against the original black.

Worn low on the hips, it sags satisfyingly under the weight of carried tools and personal effects. No two are identical. The stitching is rough but load-tested — Shelf residents trust function over finish.
functionality: Six heat-sealed pouches of varying size accommodate tools, medpacks, and personal items. Wide strap distributes carried weight across the hips. Rivets double as grip points for climbing or hauling.
what_it_says: You make do with what the city discards, and you make it work better than anything store-bought.
story_hooks: One of the pouches contains a sealed data chip that isn't the wearer's — soldered shut with unfamiliar technique.
A rivet stamped with a Ferrochem lot number connects the belt to a catastrophic factory incident three years prior.
A Shelf kid wearing this belt is stopped at a Tier 2 checkpoint — the belt's salvage origin triggers a corponation ownership flag.

physical_description.visual_profile: Wide, heavy-duty belt worn slung low across the hips, creating a utilitarian anchor point for the wearer's personal ecosystem. Reads as practical streetwear—the kind of accessory that suggests someone who carries their livelihood on their body. Silhouette is deliberately slouched and weighted.
physical_description.fit: Loose, low-slung fit across hips and upper thighs. Designed to sag under load without shifting. Adjustable via salvaged buckles to accommodate different body types and layering beneath.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged industrial conveyor-belt rubber as main strap, reinforced with reclaimed nylon webbing. Heat-sealed scrap vinyl pouches. Brass and steel rivets of mixed origin and patina.
physical_description.texture: Rubber strap has a weathered, slightly tacky surface with deep grain. Nylon webbing underneath is worn soft and frayed at edges. Vinyl pouches have a creased, supple texture from use. Rivets vary—some polished brass, some oxidized steel, all slightly proud of the surface.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant black rubber with acid-bleach streaking in pale yellow-grey creating organic, unpredictable patterns. Brass rivets add warm metallic accents; steel rivets contribute cooler grey tones. Vinyl pouches in muted greys and washed blacks.
physical_description.closures: Primary fastening via scavenged metal buckles (style varies per belt—no standardization). Pouch closures are typically friction-fit or simple friction tabs, occasionally magnetic snaps salvaged from industrial equipment.
distinctive_features: Mismatched rivets—each unique in origin, finish, and slight positioning variation
Acid-bleach patterns that are one-of-a-kind on every belt
Multiple heat-sealed vinyl pouches of varying sizes
Visible rough stitching throughout—deliberately functional, not decorative
Weight and sag characteristic of tool-laden daily use
No brand markers except subtle Patchline tag inside one pouch
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4–5 street/sub-grade. Signals working-class resourcefulness and rejection of corpo aesthetics. Expensive to replace, cheap to acquire.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Shelf residents, salvage workers, tool-users, and anyone whose profession or survival depends on carrying gear. Signals self-sufficiency, technical competence, and comfort with material scarcity. Anti-fashion statement—form follows pure function.
physical_description.condition_typical: Intentionally weathered and distressed. Worn patches of rubber, faded bleach marks, scuffs from tool contact, occasional small punctures sealed with vinyl tape. Patina increases with age and use—a Patchline belt becomes more authentic-looking the harder it's worked.
